Kārttikeya's conception is deposed under oath at ch 154 along a route ch 152 does not contain; the Avadhūteśvara episode runs beat for beat across chapters seventy-six apart, sharing two similes and the *Jīva* etymology, and the later telling calls itself the **original**; Nṛsiṃha's rage is resolved by curse-and-rehabilitation at ch 216 and by flaying at ch 241 on a shared three-element setup. Against that, three disclosure mechanisms deployed five times — kalpa-variance (163, 298), back-reference-and-decline (239), announced re-telling (286, 217). **The machinery existed, was in active use, and did not reach the four cases that needed it.** Carries two corrections: the *"disagree about whether Viṣṇu dies"* formulation withdrawn on endnote 779, and the paśu pair (179/253) held at `[n=1 OBSERVED]` with the register-reading carried

concepts.title: The Four Kinds of Devotee
concepts.description: afflicted, inquisitive, artha-seeking, jñānī, *"a succeeding category is superior."* **Ranked by contingency, not virtue** — only the last has no termination condition. And it exists to make the destruction a lesson: *"you wished to cross over saṃsāra through karma alone."* **A ranking with no ladder**

concepts.title: The Four Śaiva Paths
concepts.description: in the volume's longest chapter (4,962 words, never opened on the first pass): **Śaiva Siddhānta, the Pāśupata vow, the great vratas and the *kāpālika mode*, named and accepted** — *"as a result of Shiva's command, I have worshipped them too"* — with dakṣiṇa and the paths beyond it, *"There is no conflict with them"*, and Sāṃkhya, Vaiśeṣika, Yoga and Nyāya called *"virtuous and distinguished."* ⚑ **But the verb throughout is *permission*, not approval.** It is a clearance procedure — an enumeration of everyone who could obstruct a rite — and every grant of standing arrives welded to *"controlled by Shiva's commands."* The exclusion list that follows contains **no birth category at all**

concepts.title: The Gana Census
concepts.description: fifty-seven named gaṇa-leaders in crores, the arithmetic abandoned mid-clause. **A number that prices something and a number that lengthens something look identical on the page**

concepts.title: The Gayatri Quota
concepts.description: 1,200,000 recitations makes "a complete brahmana," under 100,000 disqualifies from Vedic rite, and thirty-one missed sandhyas means the thread ceremony is performed a second time

concepts.title: The Glance That Burst an Eye
concepts.description: Kubera looks at Umā, his eye bursts unprompted, she names it accurately — and Śiva **laughs** and rules it innocent. Four verdicts, three agreeing, and **the eye is never restored**

concepts.title: The God in Costume
concepts.description: an omniscient god in disguise **fourteen times**, and he keeps announcing that he already knew. The device produces not knowledge but **evidence that cannot be contested**, and the disclosure at the end — *"I only wanted to test you"* — is the payload. Two episodes expose what that holds together: at ch 257 the subject **passes and is eaten**, with the death assigned to his own prārabdha karma; at ch 250 Pārvatī creates the doorkeeper, wears the disguise, and punishes the response. And the one test never disclosed (ch 283) is the one that sets three worlds on fire

concepts.title: The God With No Gotra
concepts.description: asked the routine lineage question at kanyādāna, **Śiva turns his face away and says nothing**, before an assembly the text enumerates. Nārada covers the silence with a veena everyone tries to stop, then discloses the stage-management: *"Sarveshvara Shankara **urged my mind**."* **The slander was true, and it stops a rite**

concepts.title: The Goddess Assembled
concepts.description: the gods complain that the demon *"performs all these himself"*, having consolidated every divine office — and their remedy is to **consolidate themselves.** A body assembled part by part with every donor named, then a **second** operation once they notice *"she was without any weapons"*, in which each god hands over his own signature emblem. ⚑ **Read as an inventory, that paragraph is a complete iconographic disarmament of the pantheon.** And between the lion and the serpent-necklace: *"Kubera gave her a vessel filled with liquor"* — **standard issue, in a volume that lists drinking among the five great sins**, and her cult is separately prescribed liquor, flesh and fish

concepts.title: The Goddesses at the Bedchamber
concepts.description: Tulasī asks the volume's sharpest question — *"you abandoned Sati and burnt Kama down; **how did you then send Vasishtha as a messenger now?**"* — and Svāhā closes it: *"it is the practice of women from the inner quarters to prattle."* **Third disposal by renaming: pride, confusion, prattle.** And Arundhatī boasts that she manufactured Menā's consent

concepts.title: The Golden Egg Struck by Ishvara
concepts.description: it does not hatch, it is **struck** from outside, and every promise the egg image makes about maturation is cancelled by that verb. A rival cosmogony absorbed by leaving the image intact and replacing everything holding it up

concepts.title: The Grades of Emancipation
concepts.description: salokya, samipya, sarupya, sarshti, sayujya; four of the five are proximity terms, and the volume quotes the maximum nearly every time

concepts.title: The Gross and the Subtle Lingam
concepts.description: the stone is for those who *"cannot control their minds through subtle images"*; and for the knower, **"there are no rules about what should be done and what should not be done"** — granted on a self-assessment the same volume calls the innermost delusion

concepts.title: The Guru's Cow
concepts.description: **a controlled experiment nobody arranged.** Four men are responsible for a cow that is not theirs, in six chapters, and intention is the only variable. Nṛga misdirects one by honest error and **becomes a lizard**; Pṛṣadhra kills a bull mistaking it for a tiger and his guru, **explicitly finding the sin *"inadvertent and not voluntary"***, demotes him permanently out of his varṇa; Triśaṅku slaughters one deliberately in a famine, is cursed and renamed for three sins, and is then given a kingdom and bodily ascent *"While devas and Vasishtha looked on"*; seven boys kill one, launder it through a śrāddha and lie, and are **punished as cruelty and credited as a good deed in one chapter by one narrator.** ⚑ **The accidental cases draw the harshest penalties** — and the four are coherent on a variable the text never names: whose cow it was

concepts.title: The Halving of Knowledge Down the Lineage
concepts.description: the god has all of it, Vyasa half, the narrator a quarter, disclosed mid-pitch: a decay curve stated as a fraction

concepts.title: The Hells That Fit the Crime
concepts.description: the punishments run on a rule the text **states twice in general form before instancing it**: *"Whichever organ a man has used to make the wife of another suffer, that organ is made to suffer."* Nine matched instances — eyes needled for gazing, tongue nailed for eating before offering, face spiked for frowning. ⚑ **But four of the nine fall on organs of *perception*, and one punishes a man for *hearing* criticism somebody else spoke** — the correspondence extended from doing to perceiving and from agency to presence, unannounced. The facility has **two doors**, a courtesy reception at the eastern gate, **Vasiṣṭha as chief of the accounts department**, and a jurisdiction map that never once mentions the amnesty

concepts.title: The Indemnity Clause Runs Hot
concepts.description: *following the customary practices of the world*, sixteen times, and **not one covers a wrongdoing**. They cover grief, rage, agitation, wonder, weeping, sex, childcare, parental confusion. So the clause is a **theological** shim, not a moral one — protecting the claim that the god is unattached and beyond the guṇas from a story that needs him visibly moved. Ch 167 puts both halves in one sentence. **Six deployments across the eight chapters of the Gaṇeśa episode and three in the single chapter where Śiva sees Gaurī in distress**, against seven scattered across the remaining hundred and thirty — a stress gauge. Two outliers show the device decaying: one stretched to cover an act, one pure filler

concepts.title: The Inventory of What You Are Giving Away
concepts.description: Vyāsa asks *"Is there a single donation that bestows the fruits of all donations?"*, is told *"**he must donate the universe**"*, and immediately asks *"**Please tell me about the size and nature of the universe**"* — **and seven chapters of cosmography follow.** ⚑ **The Purāṇa's geography is a schedule of the thing being handed over**, and it behaves like one: extent, contents, valuation, with Pātāla given floors of gold and a testimonial — *"**Narada arrived at an assembly in heaven and reported that the nether regions are more beautiful than heaven**."* ⛔ And the transaction has a hole: **the donor owns none of it and the return is *"lordship of the seven worlds."*** What is scheduled is the extent of a renunciation — **you cannot relinquish what you have not enumerated** — and the same Saṃhitā does it again to the body, in trade weights

concepts.title: The Kailāsa Is a Different Book
concepts.description: twenty-three chapters that are a tantric ritual manual, not a Purāṇa: a 169-cell maṇḍala measured by palm leaf, bīja mantras given by alphabetic position, ordination in full procedure. **Four independent markers separate it from the Saṃhitā printed next to it** — twenty-six tattvas against ~50 **in the same rite with the same spoken formula**; five Praṇava components against four, **stated twice on each side**, which is composition rather than corruption; actual Devanāgarī breaking through the edition's transliteration policy where an argument about letters cannot survive being transliterated; and the **Śiva Sūtras cited by number and expounded**. Against which they agree exactly on burying a mendicant seated and splitting the skull with a coconut

concepts.title: The Kali Yuga Varna Audit
concepts.description: a class-by-class indictment where every charge is a boundary violation, closing on the question the next chapter answers: what is the easiest method now

concepts.title: The Kartika Therapeutic Calendar
concepts.description: ailment, day, deity, donation, with real Ayurvedic preparations in the list — every one of them donated rather than administered

concepts.title: The Ketaka Still Banned
concepts.description: *"there is no flower that is not loved by Śiva,"* except two — and the ketaka's exclusion is the sentence from ch 15, **enforced by the Saṃhitā whose own retelling contains no crime for it to punish**

concepts.title: The Khaṇḍa That Summarises Itself
concepts.description: the whole forty-three-chapter arc told in chapter one and then told again. **The volume's only deliberate doubling**, and therefore the control case for the other two

concepts.title: The Kshetra Map of Bharata
concepts.description: rivers graded by confluences and gated by Jupiter transits; a twelve-year cycle does not organize a journey, it organizes a biography

concepts.title: The Ladder From Satsang to Brahman
concepts.description: devotion traced down through worship and guru to **association with the virtuous**, then run back up; six rungs and **no counts anywhere**, so nothing can be fallen behind on

concepts.title: The Lamp He Tore His Garment For
concepts.description: **not a lamp he knocked over**: he tore his garment for a wick *"so as to get better illumination"* while robbing the temple, and died without eating what he stole. The merit is constructed at the trial

concepts.title: The Lifespans and Sadashiva's Breath
concepts.description: the pantheon ranked with no claim of greatness, only **units**: each tier's whole life is one day of the next. Then measure is refused, and *undecaying* is derived from **immeasurability**, not magnitude

concepts.title: The Lineage That Swallowed the Śākyas
concepts.description: *"Sanjaya's son will be Maya and Maya's son will be **Shakya**. **Shakya's son will be Shuddhoda**"* — the Buddha's clan and father filed in the solar dynasty with the son absent and no comment. **Absorption by cataloguing: there is nothing in a genealogical entry to disagree with.** And the word *"Buddha"* occurs **exactly once in the whole volume**, in endnote 2053, observing that a daśāvatāra list runs to nine. Against Volume 2, which folds Buddha *into* the avatāra list — **two incompatible strategies, neither acknowledging the other.** ⛔ Reported as the text's handling, never as history

concepts.title: The Liṅga Gazetteer
concepts.description: three chapters later the same compiler produces **sixty-six liṅgas in one paragraph**, six of them named twice inside it, four of them jyotirliṅgas demoted to *"the ones that are ordinary and the rest"*, and one of them the upaliṅga he had just assigned to Oṃkāra. He announces a four-direction survey and delivers it in four incompatible formats — gazetteer east, eight chapters of narrative south, a single shrine west, *"briefly"* north — with Gokarṇa appearing in two quarters, disambiguated by the word *another*. And the rewards are **generated from the names**: the moon-lord grants moon-like radiance, the siddhi-lord grants siddhi. One of these two lists is the most famous thing in Śaiva geography and the other is unread, and the difference was decided at the level of form

concepts.title: The Liṅga That Had to Be Caught
concepts.description: Dārukavana, and the volume's own account of where the liṅga came from: a god who arrives *"in a disfigured form, so as to test them"* and *"affectionate towards his devotees"*, ascetics *"deluded by Shiva's maya"* who curse the organ off him, and a severed phallus that burns Pātāla, heaven and earth because it *"did not remain stationary in any one place."* Brahmā blames the cursers; the remedy is a ritual procedure with **one irreplaceable component** — *"Other than Parvati, no one else is capable of holding my penis"*

concepts.title: The Lingam as the Fallback Path
concepts.description: introduced in its first sentence as what you do if you are "incapable of following the three means," and revalued sixteen chapters later as outweighing everything combined

concepts.title: The Lingams Vishvakarma Made
concepts.description: nineteen gods issued lingams *"according to entitlements,"* ruby down to a lingam of flour for **the shadow** — and not one objects. Brahmanas get **earth**, which reads as a snub and is the highest allocation on the list

concepts.title: The Machine and the Amnesty
concepts.description: **nineteen chapters cancel karma outright, across all four Saṃhitās, on at least five currencies** — a vrata, an accident, bare favour, austerity, death in battle — against four chapters whose rule is that *"if it is not enjoyed, it will not be exhausted, even in hundreds of crores of kalpas"* and whose jurisdiction map has **no slot for the pardoning power at all.** ⚑ **Once, the text argues.** Brahmā makes the case against a tiger in full; Devī concedes every word — *"Everything that you have said is true… Nevertheless, it has sought refuge with me"* — ⚑⚑ **and Brahmā then argues her case back for a page, ending at *"You are also the one who establishes good deeds and bad deeds"*: the categories he prosecuted under are withdrawn from underneath his own objection.** Five reconciliations in five chapters, none referencing another; and Īśvara's own account — *"I have created some rules, so that my devotees are not utterly helpless"*

concepts.title: The Mahāmṛtyuñjaya Mantra
concepts.description: the Khaṇḍa's fullest liturgy, taught **over a corpse** by **the preceptor of the asuras**, claiming to be *"stated in the śruti texts"* — and Debroy: *"**different from, and an expansion of**, the standard."* Seven triads, a relocated cucumber, and a dhyāna in which **Girijā is the only one doing anything**

concepts.title: The Māras Born From a Sigh
concepts.description: an army exhaled from Brahmā's frustration, vocabulary *"Kill. Slice."*, **named by transcribing its own noise**. The **sixth** instance of the created-being formula — and the only one spoken by a third party, because its occupants cannot

concepts.title: The March, Counted
concepts.description: crores, then *"crores and crores"*, then two leaders with **one thousand crores each**, then a summary that abandons arithmetic. **The unit dissolves and nothing downstream consumes the figure.** The army *"resembled Rudra"*; the dogs come from his body hair and the drums from his mouth — **not equipment but emission**

concepts.title: The Mare-Headed Fire, Held Until the Deluge
concepts.description: the rage outlives its target and *"desired to burn down the three worlds."* Nobody proposes extinguishing it. A storage contract instead: custodian, release date, and a feeding clause — *"its food will always be your water."* **The volume can restore the god the fire killed and cannot dispose of the fire**

concepts.title: The Mendicant's Burial
concepts.description: *"**There are no burning rites for mendicants who are emancipated**… their bodies are buried."* A ditch *"as long as a staff"* north or east of a sacred tree, shami leaves with their tips east, the body *"**in a posture of yoga and facing the east**"* with staff and kamaṇḍalu, and then *"**a coconut will be used to splinter the skull into four parts**."* ⚑⚑ **Kapāla-kriyā transposed rather than dropped** — and the Vāyavīya, which disagrees with the Kailāsa on every technical question tested, prescribes the same disposal in its own vocabulary: *"his funeral rites should not be performed the way they are undertaken for a **Pashu**."* **Divergent doctrine over a shared institutional floor.** And the destination is not final: in Śiva's own world, *"**Prakriti… brings him down with a fierce spear**"* until the residual desire burns off

concepts.title: The Monkey Face Nobody Mentions
concepts.description: he asks for *Hari's* form and gets a *hari* face; two ganas sent "to protect him" describe it in his hearing and **the correction bounces off**

concepts.title: The Morning Body
concepts.description: asked about virtue, the chapter answers with where to defecate, three or five or seven strokes of mud, and which finger not to use; a setup procedure for an instrument, and the instrument is the person

concepts.title: The Nanda Vow
concepts.description: twelve months, no two alike, **no priest, no fire, no counts and no failure clause**, performed by a girl in her own house. Named for a tithi group it barely uses, and run mostly on **Riktā** days — *"for emptiness… like cleansing"*

concepts.title: The Narrator Who Bows to No One
concepts.description: the exemption belongs to the chair, not the man, which is what lets a child temporarily outrank a room where rank is fixed at birth

concepts.title: The Nested Narrators
concepts.description: no authorial voice anywhere; every claim a report of a report, terminating in the god, which permits accretion and forbids revision

concepts.title: The Newborn Who Spoke to Her Father
concepts.description: Devī **confounds the room** to speak to Dakṣa alone, excluding her mother by name, delivers a **receipt** — *"your wishes have now been met. Continue with your austerities"* — then *"assumed the form of an infant, crying near her mother"*

concepts.title: The Niyamas of the Listener
concepts.description: initiation, ground-sleeping, celibacy, one plain meal, eighteen banned foods; renunciation you can rent in nine-day instalments

concepts.title: The Omen Catalogue
concepts.description: portents *"of the three types"*, complete coverage: falling nakṣatras at midday, **white scorpions born from meteors**, thousands of vultures that ***touch Dakṣa's head***, blood and stakes vomited. Everyone understands it. **And it names no remedy** — so Dakṣa does not fix the fault, he finds a bigger patron

concepts.title: The Once-Glossed Layer
concepts.description: a census of the volume's glossed technical vocabulary: **116 distinct terms, 111 of them appearing exactly once.** Six carry real weight — ***puryaṣṭaka*** routed up the suṣumnā through six named stations **with its eight components never enumerated**, in a text that enumerates everything; ***parivetta / parivitti***, a named offence about marrying out of birth order; ***nāḍīsandhāna***, the consciousness-transfer at initiation; and the ***avabhṛtha***, where **a goddess is instructed to become a river so the audience can bathe at the end of the Purāṇa.** ⚑ Four of the six sit in chapters no sweep and no reading pass would surface — **it takes a count to see that a word never came back**

concepts.title: The One Thing the Lens Found
concepts.description: the honest record of a pre-specified instrument. A frame-violation lens ran 304 chapters and returned **one contested hit** — *"O Umā's lord!"*, a Śaiva vocative inside a sustained Vaiṣṇava hymn at ch 186, with endnotes 353 and 354 bracketing it in silence — and ch 172 does the reverse deliberately and at length, which may make it house style rather than a seam. Everything substantive came from unplanned instruments: ch 219 announcing 108 forms and enumerating 100; ch 214's speech-tag covering two voices, needing three notes to separate them; the doublets; the construction sweeps. **The working instruments all measured features the author was not choosing.** Records the failure modes too — inline note markers defeating phrase matching, sampling on the dependent variable, and the build's own score of quotation claims 7/7 against sequence claims 0/3

concepts.title: The Palm Line That Cannot Be False
concepts.description: one inauspicious line, a groom who is naked and houseless, and a remedy that is **not escape but revaluation**: *"in him, the wicked qualities become good qualities."* The forecast comes true exactly; the family's conduct changes completely; **the two never conflict.** Menā objects and is renamed *confused*

concepts.title: The Pancha Lakshana
concepts.description: the five marks that define a Purana, three of them genealogy: the genre's definition is a fossil of its first form

concepts.title: The Parthiva Lingam
concepts.description: a handful of riverbank clay, made at dawn, gone by evening, ranked supreme by seven repetitions of "in that way"; the object that needs no custody, property or heir

concepts.title: The Pāśupata Charter
concepts.description: an order's warrant placed in the god's mouth before the current cycle of ages. Ch 179 makes **everyone in the cosmos a paśu** as a condition of the Tripura war and sells the fifteen-year release in the same speech, so Brahmā and Viṣṇu are inside the problem the order exists to solve. Ch 233–234 then run twenty-eight Vyāsas, twenty-eight avatāras and four disciples each — the total stated as 112 and **108 actually named — the seventh teacher's four are missing and no note says so** *(corrected 2026-08-11; Volume 3 enumerates the same lineage at 106 and diagnoses a lost shloka)* — landing on Lakuli, who enters an abandoned corpse in a cremation ground, initiates Kuśika, Garga, Mitra and Kauruṣya, and does it at **a place the translator locates as Kārvān in Vadodara district, where the liṅgam and temple stand today**. Twenty-seven unfalsifiable entries and one visitable address

concepts.title: The Patra Doctrine
concepts.description: the same gift pays ten years or Kailāsa depending only on who takes it; *patra* means one who saves the donor, and asking halves the return

concepts.title: The Pavilion of Artificial Gods
concepts.description: Viśvakarmā builds copies of every deity present, *"to confuse people"*, and succeeds — *"even learned people could not distinguish."* **The narrator of the entire book describes his own counterfeit in the first person**: *"I was also artificially created."* The gatekeeper's post is held by an object that cannot discriminate

concepts.title: The Penance Was to Keep Telling It
concepts.description: *"**as you continue to tell people what you have done, you will gradually be purified**… this is the prāyaścitta I have decided for you."* **The confession *is* the penance** — and it explains why Brahmā confesses this crime and deletes the other one

concepts.title: The Place Multiplier and Its Collapse
concepts.description: nine rungs at ten times each, a hundred million to one, dissolved by the last sentence; and a second ladder of times that ends with the company of the virtuous

concepts.title: The Practice Layer
concepts.description: a complete working practice — nine named mantras, seven vratas with dates, six weapons, a purpose-built counter-technique — and **the volume never once lists any of it**, though it will enumerate sixty-six liṅgas in a paragraph. Every item stays welded to its case. The strongest items carry restrictions issued at the moment of founding, and the strongest of those is kept secret **from Viṣṇu and Brahmā** — a boundary drawn inside the pantheon. And the aghorāstra is manufactured from **bhasma** by recitation, collapsing the mantra-layer and the astra-layer into one system whose raw material is the ash a Pāśupata already wears

concepts.title: The Praise That Came From Another Purana
concepts.description: Debroy's first endnote: the seven chapters arguing hardest for this text's supremacy are imported from the Skanda Purana, "since they are about the greatness of Shiva Purana"

concepts.title: The Praṇava Diagram
concepts.description: **the liṅgam as a chart.** *"'A' adhered itself to the southern side… 'U' was to the north and 'M' was in the centre. **The sound of the half-matra was heard on top of the lingam**"* — and each Veda then *"established itself in ten aspects"*, delivering guṇa, deity, function, tattva, kalā, brahman-face and **a physical position on the stone**, each stated by the Veda in the first person. ⚑⚑ The scheme manifests **during a precedence quarrel and assigns the two quarrellers the two lowest positions**, deriving *"Shiva is the supreme cause"* from a mapping rather than asserting it. ⛑ **And the fourth column will not count** — the translator concedes *"**Unlike the others, for Atharva Veda, it is impossible to precisely count which ten are meant**"* — with two further worlds, Unmanā and Soma, stacked above the scheme's own terminus

concepts.title: The Prāsāda Mantra (HAUM): Śiva's Visarga-Breath
concepts.description: "Ha" prefixed to AUM; the space between repetitions is japa

concepts.title: The Prices That Do Not Match
concepts.description: killing a man costs 700 lingams in ch 28 and 100,000 in ch 46; **every overlapping price rises**, never falls. A ratchet is not noise

concepts.title: The Puns That Carry Doctrine
concepts.description: *vara* = boon **and** groom; *tata* = son **and** father; *guru* = "large" **or** "obstructor of the guṇas." Three flagged forks, none adjudicated, each holding up something the tradition treats as settled

concepts.title: The Quarrel Over Who Is Whose Father
concepts.description: rage held behind a calm face, the diminutive returned in kind, and paternity as the only currency of divine rank

concepts.title: The Question Asked Twice
concepts.description: the same twelve-item question in two frames sixty lines apart, and the outer one never answered: a seam on the page, navigation in the room

concepts.title: The Recitation as Staged Event
concepts.description: astrologer, announcements, plantain-pillar platform, canopy, tiered seating, a comfort break, and an itemized closing bill; the text's own analogy for itself is a wedding

concepts.title: The Refuge-Duty That Binds Everyone
concepts.description: the corpus's **only unaimable principle**, and the reason is structural: it triggers on the petitioner's act, so there is no step at which merit, side or standing can be assessed. Śiva spares an enemy messenger who came to demand his wife; Śukra turns it against Śiva's own army using Śiva's own gift, and says so; a widow with nothing invokes it and it works. **And it is exploitable for exactly that reason** — Viṣṇu builds the terror, supplies the shelter, and discharges the duty perfectly while running an assault. Held against Tripura, where generations of refuge did not save anyone

concepts.title: The Register Seam at Andhaka
concepts.description: the volume's most direct statement about its own composition is printed on a chapter heading in the translator's words: *"The composition of these Andhaka chapters is quite different… Sometimes, the sentences are incomplete… some liberties have been taken."* Two survivals in the English confirm it — a subordinate clause at ch 216 with no verb, and the ch 214 attribution collapse — and the annotation itself changes character across the block, from naming referents to reconciling contradictions and filling omissions, seven such notes in twelve consecutive. **Filed deliberately as corroboration and not as discovery**, since the translator raised it first

concepts.title: The Retinue and the Order of Worship
concepts.description: a household walked from the north-east, with two horrors bracketing it; **a hierarchy a copyist cannot reorder**

concepts.title: The Righteous Demon Problem
concepts.description: the volume's own narrator says of its worst villain that *"with the exception of devas, all living beings were happy"*, and does it five times. No enemy is ever charged with misrule. **The solution is never an argument — it is an adjustment to the category**: *"though you have been born from a danava lady's womb, **you are not really a danava**"*, said of a good ruler, against *"those who belong to mleccha jatis must be killed"*, said of three cities of Śiva's own devotees. At ch 205 the messenger builds a reductio from Śiva's own premise and gets a reply that denies partiality and asserts it four sentences later

concepts.title: The Sages Made From Body Parts
concepts.description: the *mind-born* sons sourced to eyes, heart, ears, **four vital airs**, a lap and a shadow. An inconsistent taxonomy is a **stratigraphy**

concepts.title: The Saṃhitā That Grew
concepts.description: the text publishes its own weights. The original twelve Saṃhitās sum to **exactly 100,000** and the abridged seven come within **0.6%** of the printed text — but **Umā is +45.6% and Vidyeśvara −23.0% while the other five sit still**, so the scale is right and the distribution is not. And Umā is, on a completely independent instrument, the only section carrying demonstrably imported material. **The Umā grew by absorption; the Kailāsa and Vāyavīya did not grow and simply never agreed** — a distinction the budget buys and the contradictions alone could not. Carries the discovery that the same table appears in Volume 1 with two figures halved, summing to 95,500 while asserting 100,000

concepts.title: The Śarabha and the Hide
concepts.description: Nṛsiṃha's rage outlives its cause and Prahlāda's embrace fails: *"Though his heart became cool, the blaze of rage did not retreat."* The volume resolves this **twice, incompatibly** — a Saptarṣi curse and rehabilitation at Badarī (ch 216), against Vīrabhadra and the Śarabha (ch 239–241) — and flags neither, in a chapter that opens by using the back-reference device on other material. Then the extreme case of the absorption machine: destroyed, **skinned, and worn**, with his face as the chief skull in the garland, and in the same chapter declared *"the foremost among my devotees"* — having consented to the treatment mid-beating

concepts.title: The Second Column of Fire
concepts.description: the same episode as ch 13–15, narrated by **Brahmā in the first person**, and the ketakī, the lie, the false witness, Bhairava and the stripping of worship are **all absent**. Nothing anywhere says the story has been told twice

concepts.title: The Second Morning Protocol
concepts.description: three mornings, identical in sequence and almost nowhere else; what is invariant was carried in bodies, and everything that drifted was held only by the manuscript

concepts.title: The Sectarian Exclusions
concepts.description: a tantrika and two Vaiṣṇava insignia barred from the yajña; the difference is **a ninety-degree rotation** of the same three lines

concepts.title: The Seed and Shoot Circularity of Grace
concepts.description: devotion from favour, favour from devotion, stated openly and reclassified as a natural process; the doctrinal footing under every rescue in the volume

concepts.title: The Sentence That Gets Negotiated Down
concepts.description: two total sentences argued away in one chapter; neither verdict withdrawn, a compensating position granted instead

concepts.title: The Settlement, Itemised
concepts.description: a goat's head for Dakṣa, eyes **restored** to Bhaga *"so that he will behold his share"*, Pūṣan left to officiate **with broken teeth**, a goat's beard **added** to Bhṛgu, and the Aśvins' arms reassigned as mounts. **Restoration tracks function, not harm** — and the whole schedule is delivered before the inquiry. **Satī has no clause**

concepts.title: The Seven Days as a Pharmacy
concepts.description: a physician-god designs the week, one day per complaint; and "even if other devas are worshipped, it is really Shiva who bestows the fruits" — absorption rather than exclusion

concepts.title: The Seven Infertilities
concepts.description: six clinical presentations and **nalaparavartini, a woman who delivers only daughters**; childlessness redefined as sonlessness, inside a medical list

concepts.title: The Share-Grievance Migrates
concepts.description: Volume 1's Satī names two grievances, *"dishonoured **and also noticed that Rudra wasn't offered a share**"*, and the ritual one drives the plot. Volume 3 gives her a scene four times as long — a vimāna, three speeches, a curse that is fulfilled to the letter — **and the share is not in any of it.** She argues precedence instead, *"what is the kind of honour you show to me, your eldest daughter?"*, and Dakṣa answers by ranking her sisters' husbands and calling hers spiritually numb. The share-argument surfaces two chapters later in Vīrabhadra's mouth as a pleading — *"**Give us our shares. If no share has been planned for us in this sacrifice, tell us the reason for that.**"* — **and that version is answered on the merits.** ⚑ Same claim, different mouth, and only one of them counts as a claim. Second instance at ch 349, where Saṃjñā's objection to her husband's form is granted after **her substitute** states it. Carries the unflagged **60,000 vs 8,000 gaṇas** divergence across volumes

concepts.title: The Śiva Hymn Repertoire
concepts.description: kīrtana as celebration; the catalog of stotras and aṣṭakams

concepts.title: The Siddhi Cascade
concepts.description: an **eight-tier cumulative ladder announced at 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64**, enumerating exactly eight new items per tier and **writing out every carry-forward**. In a text with no numerals, it is the hardest counting task in the corpus and the one the corpus gets right — ⚑ **which is what makes the six announce/deliver failures worth anything: "the text cannot count" is not available.** And the sixty-four powers are introduced as things that ***"must be contended with"***, dismissed mid-sentence as *"only a small part"*, and given an evidential function in the yogi's own voice: *"Since I have seen this, moksha is **also** possible"*

concepts.title: The Sin List Bhasma Erases
concepts.description: killing, arson and perjury cleared; **criticizing a devotee is the one thing prayashchitta can never purify**

concepts.title: The Six Lingams
concepts.description: grown, drawn, installed, carried, taught and sounded, retrofitted onto the five parts of AUM; the guru's body enters the list as an item between two kinds of stone

concepts.title: The Six Vices
concepts.description: the only interior taxonomy here that assigns fault, and the only one never worked out in the body; its last two items require a position to acquire

concepts.title: The Sixteen Upacharas
concepts.description: call, seat, wash the feet, oil, bathe, clothe, perfume, feed, see out; a hospitality sequence applied unchanged to five gods and twelve human guests, and food is what survives every compression

concepts.title: The Slander That Śiva Wrote
concepts.description: a disparagement kit deployed **four times in twenty chapters, three of them by Śiva himself in disguise or on commission** — and Menā, who was present at none of them, reproduces its three figures **in order** (gold/glass, sandalwood/mud, sun/firefly) in genuine grief. **Unflagged by Debroy.** The build's largest find made without the translator's help `[n≥3 PATTERN]`

concepts.title: The Stacked Icon as the Whole Tradition's Trajectory
concepts.description: the Kālī-union-corpse painting read bottom-up as a totem-pole map of the whole religion

concepts.title: The Strata This Purāṇa Carries
concepts.description: **eight things in a Purāṇa that are not Purāṇic**, reported and deliberately not dated: a **13×13 maṇḍala** laid out with thread and bīja mantras given *"the third letter of the 'Sha' category, the sixth vowel"* rather than written out; **khecarī and kākī described by method and never named**; a **recursive catechism** in paśu/pāśa/pati with the five kañcukas; dīkṣā as physiology — *"he will **enter the shishya's nadi**… the consciousness, **which is like a blue dot**"*; a Śākta chain in which every deity's power is a Śakti; the **devayāna/pitṛyāna pair resolved into ten deities and then feminised**, absorbed with no attribution; and a unit of time defined as *"**when the fingers are snapped and circled around the knees**."* ⚑⚑ **And one citation worth more than the other seven combined**: *"There is a **Shivasutra** that states, '**chaitanyamatma**'… **The second Shivasutra** states, '**jnanam bandhadh**'"* — with the apparatus supplying *"revealed to **Vasugupta**."* **A named non-Purāṇic text, quoted in order, with the chapter calling itself a commentary on it**

concepts.title: The Sudarśana Is Śiva's
concepts.description: *"**my Sudarśana cakra… originated with Śiva**"* — volunteered by Viṣṇu, unprompted, while petitioned. **Nobody takes the weapon; what is removed is the entitlement to it** — and attribution survives every future success where a defeat would not

concepts.title: The Sudarśana, Worked Eight Ways
concepts.description: the most recognisable object in Vaiṣṇava iconography, taken apart **eight times**: given away, dissolved into arrows, **made with a toe**, capped by decree (*"this chakra will always be ineffective against my people"*), thrown back as an insult, pacified after attacking Śiva's own portion in ignorance, used under Śiva's command, and finally **confiscated and reissued.** ⚑ The operations **contradict each other about provenance and it costs nothing** — because what is being taken is not ownership but **jurisdiction**. The claim's securest form is a hymn and a name-litany, where it is recited rather than argued. Viṣṇu never once objects

concepts.title: The Supreme Dharmas, and Who Says Them
concepts.description: the volume names the highest dharma **eight times, in eight incompatible forms**, and **four are spoken by a character deceiving somebody at that exact moment.** The sharpest: Pārvatī names wifely fidelity supreme *in the sentence ordering it destroyed* — not hypocrisy but a specification of the target's armour. **Only two are sincere, and both are women about to die for them.** The volume writes its heretic's doctrine — *"all those with bodies are equal"*, *"non-violence is supreme dharma"* — and never rebuts a word, because attribution disposes of a claim more cheaply than refutation

concepts.title: The Suta and the Brahmana Appropriation
concepts.description: Pargiter's account of a bardic literature changing hands: one teacher, six disciples, five of them brahmanas, and afterwards every addition entered from the new side

concepts.title: The Swallowing of Śukra
concepts.description: Śiva taught the daityas' guru to revive the dead and *"kept a secret from Hari and Hiranyagarbha"*; when it is used on his own troops his only remedy is to eat the man, *"like a fruit."* Śukra names the impropriety himself and does it anyway on the refuge-duty — the one principle in the volume that binds both sides. A hundred years inside, *"just as a crooked person does not find a weakness in a pure person"*, then out through the penis, renamed for it and adopted. **And the volume's largest sectarian claim arrives as scenery**: Nārāyaṇa's world, itemised among the sights inside Śiva's stomach

concepts.title: The Taxonomy of Transgressive Women
concepts.description: svairiṇī and kāminī differ by **one variable, the partner's varna** — the same axis as the chandala rule, from the other end of the act, and neither list mentions the man

concepts.title: The Taxonomy That Will Not Sort
concepts.description: six classificatory cuts of bhakti in four sentences, none composing, one with **a number and no contents**, and *"described elsewhere."* **Five vocabularies stacked; exactly one worked out**

concepts.title: The Test That Śiva Commissioned
concepts.description: the prize authors the exam: *"**use deceitful words and be harsh**."* The sages defame **Śiva's own messenger** — *"Narada's atman is full of filth"* — and inside the commissioned lie sits **a fifth account of the abandonment, the most damning in the volume**: *"finding a taint in her, the lord himself gave her up"*

concepts.title: The Thirds of Income
concepts.description: a third to dharma, a third reinvested, a third to enjoyment; a tenth off the top for agriculture because ploughing kills, and half of any windfall

concepts.title: The Thirteen Samskaras
concepts.description: nine of thirteen rites before age fifteen and none between graduation and death; item three is *pumsavana*, engendering a male child, as a **scheduled step**

concepts.title: The Three Hardships
concepts.description: trouble sorted by where it came from, never by desert; smallpox filed with lightning and nightmares because none of them has an author

concepts.title: The Three Kinds of Bhakti
concepts.description: pure, fruit-seeking, and mixed; the body invokes the count constantly and the list survives only in an endnote, and the third term is where nearly everyone lives

concepts.title: The Three Shivayogis
concepts.description: kriyā, tapas, japa read as a menu and built as a cumulative ladder, which quietly carries the bottom rung's wealth requirement all the way up

concepts.title: The Three Stages of Karma
concepts.description: seed, increase, enjoyment; jnana destroys the first, ritual reduces the second, and for the third **"even crores of good deeds will not suffice"**

concepts.title: The Three Tiers of Ritual Failure
concepts.description: reduced, futile, harmful — run consistently across nine chapters and never named; "great harm" is reserved for a portable stone made of two pieces, and intention appears in no tier

concepts.title: The Tīrtha Launders Anything
concepts.description: the instrument reads acts and never intentions, in both directions: at ch 277 a cow costs out a murder in advance (*"there is a place in this world where one can destroy the sin… I have seen that spot"*), is argued out of it on flawless karmic grounds by her own calf, proceeds, and is right; at ch 280 a starving blind woman performs a vrata by throwing away leaves she cannot eat and is credited in full, *"Though she did this involuntarily."* **But the title's claim holds only on the sin axis** — ch 238 and ch 281 both show generic tīrtha-bathing failing outright, a god carrying brahma-hatyā through *all* the tīrthas and a king exhausting japa, vrata and sacrifices, because the failures are what establish the rating of the one address that works. Set against ch 260, where Śiva itemises four lives' misfortunes against four specific prior acts, including a life ended early for an interrupted pūjā. **Neither system anywhere acknowledges the other**, and the contradiction is preserved. Carries brahma-hatyā as a speaking devotee pursuing her own liberation, who refuses Viṣṇu's direct request and is expelled by a border rather than dissolved

concepts.title: The Twelve Gifts
concepts.description: a pharmacology of donation with no quantities anywhere: gold to the digestive fire, silver to semen — and a daughter, filed eleventh, returning liberation while living

concepts.title: The Twelve Jyotirliṅgas
concepts.description: the list arrives as a memorisable verse **with its recitation-reward already attached**, before a single story is told; twenty chapters then supply those stories in a different saṃhitā, in **exactly the shloka's order, twelve for twelve**. Across the same span a name drifts three ways (Amareśvara / Parameśvara / Oṃkāreśvara), two of the twelve end at addresses nobody can now locate — precisely the two whose slots named a forest and a region rather than a city — and the upaliṅga list closes at nine of twelve with a completion formula. **Sequence is the most robust carrier; labels and referents degrade.** Also carries ch 272's opening declaration that liṅgas are infinite and unlistable, four sentences before the canonical twelve

concepts.title: The Twilights Are Her Body
concepts.description: made **invisible** so she can walk into a working priesthood's fire unseen, *"burnt along with the cakes, her fragrance unnoticed"*; Sūrya divides her in two and **the evening half feeds the ancestors her presence produced**

concepts.title: The Two Ganas Who Did Not Curse Back
concepts.description: cursed for telling the truth they were sent to tell; *"silence means life"*; and the volume's unstated rule — **utterances are irreversible, and mercy works by supplementation**

concepts.title: The Two Gautama Accounts
concepts.description: the same sage, grain, blade of grass and instant death, told twice with opposite endings — and **the text notices**. The listeners raise the discrepancy, Sūta answers *"That is also true. These differences occur because incidents have occurred in different kalpas"*, and narrates the variant in full. **The volume's four disclosure mechanisms exist, are used four times, and are used on none of its real doublets.** The endings differ because the fraud has a different author in each: Gaṇeśa argues against the frame-up, loses, and **becomes the cow himself**; in the second version the brahmanas build an artificial one. The second ends in a hereditary curse — reported here as the text's own polemic, never as description

concepts.title: The Two Wives Who Were the Weak Point
concepts.description: Pārvatī names wifely fidelity the highest dharma on earth **in the sentence ordering its destruction**; the second operation is glossed upward instead, *"Hari followed the instructions of Shiva and the mother of the universe."* Vrindā is sold a **manufactured bereavement** and detects it afterwards; Tulasī is sold a **staged victory return** and detects it *during*, by felt discrepancy — *"the happiness caused to her deviated from the normal"* — and asks. Her unanswered question is the volume's sharpest: *"how was a devotee killed, though he had committed no crime?"* **Carries the `[FALSIFIED]` obituary for the supposed tulasī origin-doublet**

concepts.title: The Vātūlanātha Sūtra: Aphorisms of the Intoxicated God
concepts.description: Śiva as Bātula Nāth, the drunk lord; intoxication as a refined category

concepts.title: The Veda-Praṇava: AUM as First Pañcākṣarī
concepts.description: A/U/M/Bindu/Nāda ↔ the Māṇḍūkya five states

concepts.title: The Vedas Testified and Were Overruled
concepts.description: Brahmā and Viṣṇu nominate the Vedas as proof and undertake in advance to accept the finding: *"We will accept what you cite as proof."* All four testify for Rudra; Praṇava assumes a body to answer their objection. **They reject it by declaring the witnesses senseless** and substituting a criterion about the defendant's appearance. Then Bhairava takes the fifth head with the nails of his left hand — *"the limb that caused the offence is the one that must be chastised"* — and both gods believe within a sentence. **The resulting sin is issued, not incurred**: Śiva generates brahma-hatyā afterwards, as a public demonstration, with its release condition specified in the same breath

concepts.title: The Vertical Cosmos
concepts.description: 14, 14, 28, 56 worlds at ten million japas a tier, all of them *below* the disappearance line; the stack is the denominator the counting apparatus needs

concepts.title: The Vocative That Does Not Fit
concepts.description: *"O great sage!"* with no sage in the room, and Debroy names its owner: **meant for Nārada, two frames out.** Both flagged violations sit in Śiva's innermost quoted speech, and **both pair with a numerical failure**

concepts.title: The Vrata He Did Not Know He Was Doing
concepts.description: a hunter waiting to shoot deer dislodges water and bilva leaves onto an unnoticed liṅgam **four times, in the vigil's four watches, with its correct offerings.** The deer plead and he *"was filled with wonder"* — ⚑ **and the very next clause credits the worship instead.** Śiva calls it ***"your vrata"***, which closes off every reading in which the merit is somebody else's. ⚑⚑ And the volume does not apologise for the accident: ***"Despite having observed the vrata involuntarily, he obtained sayujya. What need be said of the auspicious ones who immerse themselves in intense devotion?"*** — **the involuntariness is the minor premise of an *a fortiori* argument**, four lines before Śivarātri is ranked above every tīrtha, gift, sacrifice and japa

concepts.title: The Wandering Mendicant: Move Every Three Days
concepts.description: keep moving so no attachment forms; the year-round mode the monsoon interrupts

concepts.title: The Water That Came Out of Vishnu
concepts.description: the cosmic ocean is **sweat**, declared sin-destroying in the next clause; he falls asleep on it and takes his name from it; and the twenty-four tattvas assemble while he is unconscious

concepts.title: The Woman Who Legislated Puberty
concepts.description: four quarters, **desire in the third**, *"established in the world."* The volume's only rule with **no escape clause**, and its only cosmological claim anyone can check

concepts.title: "Real Ass God": The World as Real and Good
concepts.description: turning the page to learn the story; the world is real and good because it's how God reads Himself

concepts.title: The Yogi's Limbs and Impediments
concepts.description: **ten impediments, each defined**, including ailments from *"imbalance in constituents that make up the body"* and *"doubt about the place… should it be this or that?"*; **six *upasargas*, each defined**, five of them sensory upgrades filed as obstacles. Plus the only sentence in three volumes treating practitioner capacity as finite — *"**A person who is tired of japa, must perform dhyana. A person who is tired of dhyana, must perform japa**"* — a mātrā defined by **snapping the fingers**, prāṇāyāma overdose described as sweating, tremor, weeping and collapse, and samādhi given as **the exact inverse of the six upasargas**

concepts.title: The Yuga Arithmetic
concepts.description: 12,000-year cycles, 71.4 per manvantara, and a cosmology built on offices rather than persons: Indra, Manu and Vedavyasa are all job titles

concepts.title: The Yuga Method Shift
concepts.description: dhyana, tapas, yajna, image-worship: three past-tense reports and one present-tense instruction, which makes it a routing table rather than a lament

concepts.title: There Is No Difference Between You and Rudra
concepts.description: parity by decree with **mutual hell clauses**, each god policing his own devotees — and then, offered as a *secret*, the clause that undoes it: two of you came from Prakṛti and Rudra did not

concepts.title: They Agreed to Fight
concepts.description: Vīrabhadra threatens Viṣṇu at length; Viṣṇu *"was pleased and **smiled**."* Then: *"**I said that to test your sentiments**… you are just like Śiva… nevertheless, **urged, we speak to each other without affection**."* And Viṣṇu sets the choreography and his own exit — *"strike me all over my body, I will return to my own hermitage."* **Chapter 89 then delivers it and reports it straight**

concepts.title: Three Incompatible Origin Accounts
concepts.description: a man compiled it from old songs / Brahma composed it / Shiva stated it; the real conflict is compilation versus revelation

concepts.title: Three Orders of Bound Souls
concepts.description: vijñānakala / pralayākala / sakala — by which malas still bind

concepts.title: Three Sāmbas
concepts.description: one episode told a hundred and eight chapters and two Saṃhitās apart, disagreeing on the place, the initiation, the interval, the boon count and **who the child is** — the cursed Saṃvartaka sun in one, Jāmbavatī's son in the other. ⚑ **And the finding is referential rather than stylistic.** The Vāyavīya version opens *"Vasudeva Krishna… went and met **Dhoumya's elder brother** and performed **Pashupata vrata**… **We have heard this earlier**"* — and Dhaumya occurs five times in the volume, **all five in the Vāyavīya**, while *Pāśupata* does not occur in the Umā telling at all. **It cross-references itself correctly and does not know the other version exists.** Then endnote 1918 supplies a third identity, unhedged: *"Guha was born as Samba"* — and *Guha* is also the name Śiva gives a hunter sixteen chapters earlier

concepts.title: Three Modes of Japa: Yogic / Jñāna / Bhakti
concepts.description: one mantra, three temperaments; the syllable-by-syllable readings

concepts.title: Tripundraka
concepts.description: three strokes carrying twenty-seven correspondences including the three Vedic śrauta fires: **the rite is not performed, it is worn**

concepts.title: Tripura, the Hardest Case
concepts.description: *"In every house, there was a temple to Rudra… the dharma loved by Shiva was always followed."* They name Śiva as their only permitted killer **because they trust him**. He refuses — *"there is no atonement for an ingrate"* — and the text never settles who authored the corruption: **Śiva names Viṣṇu and Nārada; Brahmā names Śiva.** Then *"those who belong to mleccha jatis must be killed"*, and total annihilation, one named survivor, and a whole exempted class, three sentences apart

concepts.title: Two Boats, Two Rocks
concepts.description: *"**Two boats can carry each other across. Two rocks cannot carry each other across.** Thus, if the guru is one who is a guru only in name, **emancipation will also be in name**"* — the defect propagating to the product exactly. The chapter issues a **specification**, a **selection test** and, found nowhere else in three volumes, a **warranty**: *"**If no bliss or enlightenment is experienced even after a year, the shishya must seek refuge with another guru**"*, mandatory, measured by the disciple's own experience. ⚑⚑ **In the same passage he may not sit where he chooses and goes to Rourava hell for a word against the guru** — selection and review are his; conduct is not

concepts.title: Two Etymologies for Umā
concepts.description: the name means *"Oh! Don't!"* and the volume supplies **two incompatible origins for it, fifteen chapters apart**, both marked as *the* origin, neither acknowledging the other. **Debroy, who flags inconsistencies constantly in this same endnote range, walks past it** — the build's first unflagged narrative doublet `[n=1 OBSERVED]`

concepts.title: Two Hells, Two Shadows, Two Tattva Counts
concepts.description: the hells sit **below** the nether regions at ch 322 and *"**above** the nether regions"* at ch 330, with a grid on one side and a flat list on the other. A headless shadow means death in a month at ch 339 and loss of speech in six at ch 342 — **same speaker, same listener, one unbroken conversation.** And the Virajā oblation is performed in two Saṃhitās with **the same spoken sentence**, purifying twenty-six tattvas *"ending with Purusha"* in one and about fifty that run past him into Māyā, Sadāśiva and Śiva-tattva in the other. Praṇava settles the species: **five components in the Kailāsa, stated twice; four in the Vāyavīya, stated twice** — each side internally consistent, and corruption produces scatter rather than two coherent positions. ⭐ Plus the case found by chasing a line reference: **ch 374 and ch 419 are ninety per cent the same paragraph**, and inside it *"the **five** kinds of jnana"* against *"the **ten**"*, each glossed to fit its own number by an editor whose neighbouring notes are word-identical

concepts.title: Two Kauśikīs
concepts.description: one goddess, two origins: *"directly emerged from **the sheaths in the body**"* while the devas sing, against *"cast aside her **outer skin**"* mid-austerity at Brahmā's request, the discarded skin becoming Kauśikī and Kālī. Emergence from within against production from what was removed; independent against commissioned. ⚑ **The Vāyavīya tells its version twice and agrees with itself**, so this is two coherent traditions rather than scatter — **and ch 412 declines to re-narrate a battle *"since this has been narrated elsewhere"* in the same chapter where it supplies an incompatible origin**

concepts.title: Two Manuals That Do Not Agree
concepts.description: **north in one Saṃhitā and south in the other**, eight rinses against sixteen, and the two Rudra chapters disagreeing with *each other* two apart in one voice. North and south are not a matter of tone

concepts.title: Two Numbering Systems That Are Not Unique
concepts.description: the citation-integrity page. **362 names two chapters, 388 names two — one the Kailāsa's last and one the Vāyavīya's first — and 365 names none**, while endnote numbers restart per section so *"note 12"* is two notes. The running chapter number is the translator's own device, the Saṃhitā-internal numbering is exact throughout, and **neither hazard is stated anywhere in 2,124 notes.** The remedy is a citation form: `388-8.1(1)`, never "ch 388," and every endnote with its line reference

concepts.title: Unpredictable, Therefore Uncontrollable
concepts.description: why he is scary: not death, not asura-ness, but unpredictability; a category is the handle by which a thing is controlled; the music-genre/record-label boardroom

concepts.title: Upavāsa: Fast Only If It Nourishes
concepts.description: the anti-austerity reframe — add more japa rather than subtract food; honor the body that has to serve

concepts.title: Uṣā, and the Sentence Passed in Advance
concepts.description: Pārvatī names the month, the fortnight, the lunar day and the sleeping, a chapter before it happens; her own māyā carries the man in and **her own attendants carry him back out**. The ruling gives two incompatible reasons in one breath — punishment for wearing her form, *and* the fruit of lifelong devotion to Viṣṇu. The occasion for the impersonation was Śiva's own stated arousal, and nothing attaches to him. Then a friend supplies a prior sin, and *"she realized that everything had occurred according to the former account"* — after which the grievance never returns. Her father receives the same device: told the omen of his own ruin, he waits for it and is **delighted** when it comes

concepts.title: Vasanta From a Breath
concepts.description: spring **exhaled** while planning a seduction, assigned to a person rather than a task; and a structural objection answered four times with resource

concepts.title: Vīrabhadra and Mahākālī From One Hair
concepts.description: Śiva **sends for a second witness before acting** — the only verification in the whole Khaṇḍa. Then a strand of hair, thrown at a mountain, splits: Vīrabhadra from one half, **Mahākālī from the other**, who gets no instruction and no name at her most vivid moment

concepts.title: Vishnu Created to Bear the Burden
concepts.description: the motive stated in direct speech: *"we will be able to enjoy ourselves in Ānandavana, with our minds not agitated."* A delegate made from a tenth portion of the left side, who has to **ask for a name and a task**

concepts.title: Viṣṇu in the Brahmana's Disguise
concepts.description: he *"resorted to deception"* and is named in one minute. Then the move worth watching: **he praises the man who exposed him and shrinks the ask to a performance** — *"at least once, you should say that you are frightened."* Refused, he escalates; a fistful of **kuśa grass** becomes a trident and heaven runs

concepts.title: Viṣṇu Knew and Went Anyway
concepts.description: *"as a result of his curse, I and the lords of the gods **will be destroyed at Dakṣa's sacrifice. But I will rise up again**"* — said before any of it, then he commits to the course that produces it. **The fifth accurate forecast in the Khaṇḍa and the one that removes the last variable.** And the sharpest line in it: *"I did not leave **swiftly**"*

concepts.title: Vishnu Rewarded for Not Lying
concepts.description: permanent parity of worship for one accurate report about an event only he witnessed; the ambition explicitly overlooked, not forgiven

concepts.title: Viṣṇu Tells Brahmā He Hates Śiva
concepts.description: *"**taking Śaṅkara to be an ordinary god, you hate him**… you think of Parameśvara Rudra as your own son."* The volume's fullest doctrinal statement, put in Viṣṇu's mouth — and **metabolised into the pitch** one chapter later

concepts.title: Viṣṇu the King vs Śiva the Outcast
concepts.description: Viṣṇu's kingly, dharma-restoring avatāras vs the derelict sadhu and mad dancer; Śiva gives the boons Viṣṇu must then incarnate to undo

concepts.title: Vyasa Who Could Not Get There
concepts.description: the compiler, anxious on a riverbank: "I have become a guru to everyone. But… I do not know how that can be brought about"

concepts.title: What Is the Need for Rudra?
concepts.description: Dakṣa's real argument is **redundancy, not contempt**: the roles are staffed, so *"what is the need for Rudra?"* **The refutation exists and was delivered to a gaṇa in private, one chapter earlier**

concepts.title: What Makes an Argument Win
concepts.description: **two winners in three hundred chapters, and neither wins by being right.** Both convert the request into a citation the opponent cannot repudiate — the Vedas' truth-value (Gaṇeśa, 169) and Śiva's own prior teaching (Ghuṣmā, 304). The volume proves it with an internal control in its final chapter: **the same woman's moral appeal fails and her citation succeeds, four lines later.** Against them, the cow who grants every premise of a flawless argument — *"I know this, but maya does not let go of me"* — and kills a man the next morning. **⚑ ch 301 removed: Śiva concedes before Pārvatī argues**

concepts.title: What the Demon Knew
concepts.description: the volume's most accurate theology is spoken by the villain about the goddess killing him. **Four claims, four correct**, each independently confirmed elsewhere — and he attacks because *"if I withdrew from the battle, in front of the king of asuras, how will I show my face?"* ⚑ **Kauśikī names the mechanism in the next line, as a law: *"when hardship is imminent, the mind follows a contrary direction."*** Sixth instance of the corpus's forecast-spine and the only one whose reasoning is given in full — so it supplies the term the others could not: **shame, not orders.** He is liberated anyway

concepts.title: When He Comes and Asks for Alms
concepts.description: Dakṣa frames the bestowal as **bhikṣā**: *"when Śambhu comes and asks me for alms, I will give my daughter to him."* Śiva complies at the correct muhūrta — **wearing every ornament Dakṣa will later call disgusting**

concepts.title: Who May Be Initiated
concepts.description: **three incompatible answers, none acknowledging the others.** *"Irrespective of varna or ashrama, women, children, male servants, female servants"* at ch 309, and *"regardless of whether he is **antyaja**"* at ch 434 — against *"following Shiva's dharma, **men are divided into three varnas**"* at ch 388. And a third architecture at ch 437 in which access is **derivative**: *"**On their own, women do not possess the rights**… **a woman without a husband must seek the son's permission. With the father's permission, a maiden obtains the right**"* — a complete chain of male permission with no terminal case. ⚑ Śūdras are not barred but **substituted**: *"Sins can be cleansed by offering **padodaka**."* The probation is graded inversely — a year for a brahmana, three for a vaiśya — and the qualifying test is stated cruelty: *"**Superior shishyas will be given inferior tasks**… when they are scolded and beaten, if they are not miserable, they are worthy."* ⛑ One inherited attribution withdrawn: **ch 430 contains no varṇa term at all**

concepts.title: Who May Say What Mantra
concepts.description: the act opened to everyone and the **words** stratified by two orthogonal grids with no precedence rule

concepts.title: Whole Narratives Annexed
concepts.description: six of the surrounding literature's most famous **rescue scenes**, absorbed without disputing anything: the Kena yakṣa, Ambarīṣa, Rāma's crossing, Nala and Damayantī, Uttarā's womb, and Draupadī's garments — the last reassigned in **four words inside a list**. The plots survive; only the agent in the decisive clause changes. **No rival text is ever named**, so no claim is made that anyone could answer. And the selection is deliberate: Varāha and Nṛsiṃha are left completely alone, because their outcome is a killing rather than a saving

concepts.title: Why a Swan and a Boar
concepts.description: the swan was chosen for **discrimination** and lost it: *"how can jñāna be generated in a person who wishes to embark on the task of creation?"* The column-of-fire failure as structural, not moral

concepts.title: Why Selvalingam Distrusts Bhakti: The Case for Jñāna
concepts.description: the three dangers of bhakti; "the broad daylight of reason"

concepts.title: Why Śiva Is God: The Destroyer Argument
concepts.description: the Śivajñānabodham case: only the destroyer can create, because destruction is reabsorption, and reabsorption implies a source

concepts.title: Women and Shudras Must Be Invited
concepts.description: an exclusion named and reversed in one sentence, with a pedagogical reason and no argument; the same chapter then floors the entrance with eleven unmarked rules

concepts.title: Worse Than Death to Go Uninvited
concepts.description: he states the mechanism of her death to her face as a general rule, and names the real weapon — *"**people are not hurt by arrows shot by enemies as much as** they are hurt when their hearts are pierced by wicked words uttered by **one's own**"* — while *"pierced **yet again** by the arrows of Dakṣa's words." *Then: *"you must certainly go"*

concepts.title: Worship by Varna, Again
concepts.description: asked how the four varnas should worship, the chapter answers with **handfuls of earth and the length of your toothbrush**, graded by birth, in an act nobody can witness. A rule nobody can check is an identity mechanism

concepts.title: Worship Me First, or Nothing Counts
concepts.description: a rule that ranks nobody and forbids nothing, and is stronger than either: *"if others are worshipped without he being worshipped, **the fruits will be destroyed**."* Five bases, and **every holder was injured into the position** — a beheaded son, a being made to eat itself, a god's assassin, a class descended from a cursed man. **Enforced once against Śiva himself**, blocked at full draw for a hundred thousand years until he worships the son he decapitated — after which the narrator patches the scene unprompted. All four holders are **doorkeepers**, and the rule is that post transposed into ritual sequence

concepts.title: Worship to Prevent Birth — The Naivedya of a Lifetime
concepts.description: a meal offered thirty-six thousand times, in units built entirely of twelves, on the anniversaries of your own birth, because "the offering of the naivedya of a lifetime is like offering up one's own life"

concepts.title: Yama Outranked and Silent
concepts.description: the judge of the dead works out what happened, is frightened, worships the men who did it, and asks nothing; the karmic system informed and declining to enforce

concepts.title: Yama's Standing Order
concepts.description: the judge of the dead instructs his servants never to collect anyone in ash, rudrākṣa or matted hair — ***"even if people don Śiva's garb in insolence or in deceit."*** Insignia as jurisdiction, not purification

concepts.title: You Are Not a Man or a Woman
concepts.description: the hymn that opens the negotiation strips species, **sex (all three terms) and existence itself** — then furnishes the room it cleared, and the one local item in the residue is *"you are the three Śaktis"*

concepts.title: You Are Prakṛti, I Am Puruṣa
concepts.description: she runs Sāṃkhya against his Vedānta and lands it: *"**If you are superior to Prakriti, why are you tormenting yourself through austerities?**"* His reply relocates rather than refutes. **The narrator scores it a draw — *"there is no difference between them"* — and the plot scores it a loss**, then prescribes three thousand years of austerity

concepts.title: Your Mouth Was an Instrument
concepts.description: he asks for a penance and receives a metaphysics; **the absolution is what makes the curse permanent**, since the only person who could unsay it is told he never said it

concepts.title: A Bad Son Is Better Than a Good One
concepts.description: the argument requires the son's presence and its author leaves that night

concepts.title: A Chain of Praise
concepts.description: the volume's widest claim delivered as an epithet inside a bow, where nothing has to be reconciled

concepts.title: A City With Nine Gates
concepts.description: not a correspondence-list but a floor plan, with directions, escorts and destinations

concepts.title: A Hundred Thousand Yakṣas
concepts.description: ⚠ collective punishment named by Manu, victims called innocent, and the volume canonises both

concepts.title: A Hundred Years Like an Instant
concepts.description: a century unmonitored rather than compressed, in a volume that elsewhere counts every year

concepts.title: A Ladder You Are Meant to Leave
concepts.description: ten chapters of construction, then the teacher calling both forms products of māyā

concepts.title: A Life Told in the Future Tense
concepts.description: a war the listener's family fought, forecast to him in the future tense, with the agents demoted to apparent names

concepts.title: A Marriage Scheduled in Advance
concepts.description: the date, the bride, the nine children and the tenth-as-deity, all fixed before the asker has met anyone

concepts.title: A Share From Now On
concepts.description: the settlement is a permanent line item, and the antagonist ends with more than he began with

concepts.title: A Sixth of Their Merit and All of Their Sin
concepts.description: a fraction up and everything down, on one checkable variable

concepts.title: A Tense Repaired With the Receipt Left In
concepts.description: the volume's smallest intervention and its only fully auditable one

concepts.title: A Thousand-Year Sacrifice With Death in Attendance
concepts.description: the frame: a rite aimed at heaven, interrupted to ask a bard where dharma went, with Death seated at the fire so nobody can die

concepts.title: A Two-Muhūrta Window to Kill In
concepts.description: the text's figure against the received one, with the apparatus reporting both and settling neither

concepts.title: Acintya-Bheda-Abheda — The Gauḍīya Position
concepts.description: inconceivable simultaneous oneness-and-difference; the school's own resolution of the identity/relationship problem

concepts.title: Adhikṛta, Āśrita, Pāriṣada, Anuga — The Four Servants
concepts.description: emotional attainment capped by office, with worldly rank and available love running in opposite directions

concepts.title: Advaita Vedānta (Śaṅkara): The Position Bhakti Was Built to Refuse
concepts.description: the strict non-dualist floor the whole spectrum measures itself against

concepts.title: After Every Proximate Resource Is Named
concepts.description: the rescue waits not for exhaustion but for an itemised inventory, because an unaddressed appeal cannot be made while a recipient still seems plausible

concepts.title: Ahaitukī Bhakti: The Motiveless Ideal
concepts.description: devotion sought for no reason beyond itself, not as a means to any further end

concepts.title: Ajāmila and the Accidental Syllable
concepts.description: a lifetime of crime undone by four syllables shouted at a child who happened to be named Nārāyaṇa

concepts.title: All Conception Is Idolatry (Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura)

concepts.title: Sixteen Years Old and Nobody Covered Themselves

concepts.description: the root text and the commentary give different orders on facing pages, and the term the compression drops is the one that does not fit its axis

concepts.description: why the path begins with the ear, not the will

concepts.title: Strictly Speaking, Vidura Was Not a Śūdra
concepts.description: the apparatus contradicting the narrative's own premise, in a single subordinate clause

concepts.title: Sukṛti — The Two Kinds of Merit
concepts.description: two closed currencies of merit, each spent in its own denomination, neither convertible into devotion

Text 27's reclassification of them as transitory states is therefore an entailment, not a reversal, and the book presents it as a considered dissent from Bharata Muni.

concepts.title: Tādātmya — The Iron Rod and the Fire
concepts.description: holds that material senses cannot perform devotion at all — the capacity is borrowed, and the senses contribute only availability. Bhakti Is Produced Only by Bhakti admits forced material sense-engagement into the category, on the argument that gathering firewood is part of the sacrifice. Each is the other's counterexample, and they sit a page apart in the same Text without cross-reference. Preserved.

concepts.title: Tapas Is the Substance, Not the Technique
concepts.description: austerity placed among persons, among possessions, and called the wealth of those who own nothing

concepts.title: Ten Thousand Ears
concepts.description: the volume's only additive request, for equipment rather than a state

concepts.title: The Accretion Model: Śānta to Mādhurya
concepts.description: makes each rasa retain every prior quality on the ether-to-earth pattern, which requires all five to share a `viṣayālambana`. concepts.title: The Acquittal He Refuses
concepts.description: Yudhiṣṭhira is handed a valid exemption for righteous killing and declines to use it

concepts.title: The Ādi Clause — What "And So On" Excludes
concepts.description: two words that exclude classical yoga and sāṅkhya from the category without calling either false

concepts.title: The Adviser They Called a Servant
concepts.description: a solicited counsel destroyed by three sentences about the counsellor, answered by a bow set down at the door

concepts.title: The Anartha Taxonomy — Sixteen Plus Four
concepts.description: four classes of obstruction by four, plus four by origin, and the fourth origin is devotional practice itself

concepts.title: The Animals Are Waiting for You
concepts.description: the charge stated before the allegory and executed after it; the teaching is the wrapper

concepts.title: The Arithmetic That Does Not Fit
concepts.description: seven mothers against eighteen wives, a failed check reported and then routed around

concepts.title: The Asuras Are Devotees Too

concepts.title: The Asymmetry of Pūrva-Rāga

concepts.title: The Avadhūta Who Is Also an Outcast
concepts.description: one Sanskrit word for both transcendence and social exclusion, and the text's refusal to say which one Śuka is

concepts.title: The Avatāra Who Lies
concepts.description: a descent whose stated purpose is to make correct practitioners believe what is not dharma, and the deception eight entries earlier

concepts.title: The Bandhu Family
concepts.description: a suffix that concedes every fact of membership and withholds the membership, with no criteria anywhere

concepts.title: The Bhāgavata as Vyāsa's Own Commentary on the Vedānta Sūtra
concepts.description: the canon-legitimating move that makes the Bhāgavata's claims outrank rival Purāṇas

concepts.title: The Blank Cheque That Does Not Work

concepts.title: The Blanket Disclosure
concepts.description: one endnote conceding that simplification operated across three whole chapters, honest and unactionable at once

concepts.title: The Bliss of Bhakti Exceeds Brahman: Graded Soteriologies

concepts.title: The Buck and the Doe

concepts.title: The Chakra That Will Not Stop

concepts.title: The Chariot Decoded

concepts.title: The Compatibility Matrix and Virasatā
concepts.description: , `śānta`, `dāsya`, `sakhya`, `vātsalya` and `mādhurya` all list `raudra` incompatible; `raudra` as host rejects only `mādhurya`. So the most permissive host is the least welcome guest — and the anger material's every worked example takes place inside a primary relationship. The only route back is Text 26's *inclusion*, which is absorption rather than combination.

concepts.title: The Creator Who Cannot Find His Own Root

concepts.title: The Daughter Nobody Would Marry

concepts.title: The Dead Child Disowns His Parents

concepts.title: The Death Sentence Received as a Favour

concepts.title: The Demon Teaches the God to Fight

concepts.title: The Eight Limbs, and the Ones This Text Walks Past

concepts.title: The Massacre He Planned at a Deathbed

And the *Bindu*'s technical doctrine of separation-as-rasa is not what The Vision Granted Once and Then Withheld describes; Nārada is *"dissatisfied and afflicted"* and is handed an instrument, not an emotional achievement. **Preserved on both sides. Neither layer is corrected against the other.**

concepts.title: The Thigh That Carried the Sins

concepts.title: The Thirty-Two Sevā-Aparādhas

concepts.description: , Malam as Material Substance). Wallis's nondual Kaula reading declares mala is **ignorance** — a limited perception relinquishable in any instant, with no substance to remove (The Three Malas, Āṇava-Mala). Wallis even hands you the cataract image as the dualist position he rejects. These cannot both be literally true; each carries its whole stream's logic (ritual/officiant vs. gnosis/liberated-guru). Preserved as a live sectarian split, **not** harmonized. The slim reconciliation worth testing: cataract = the householder-therapeutic register; ignorance-mala = the gnostic-recognition register. A further layer: the same contradiction frames the **Wallis↔White** dispute (endnote 126: Wallis charges White's *Sinister Yogis* / *Kiss of the Yoginī* with "confirmation bias") over whether the historical yogī was a liberation-seeker or a power-seeker — see Yoga and Tantra History Hub.
